key_concepts: A mutation is a change in the DNA base sequence.
DNA is made of nucleotides with four bases: adenine, thymine, guanine, and cytosine.
Genes carry protein-making instructions in their nucleotide sequence.
Cells repair most mutations quickly; somatic mutations affect only that cell lineage.
Germline mutations can be passed to offspring.
Point mutations change a single DNA base and may be missense, nonsense, or silent.
Missense mutations change one amino acid; nonsense creates a premature stop codon; silent
Substitution mutations exchange one base and can cause disorders such as sickle cell anemi

Chromosomal mutations involve large DNA segments, including deletion, inversion, duplicati
Mutations can be beneficial, harmful, or neutral.
Factors that cause mutations include infectious agents, radiation, and chemicals.
